ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure gives two groups of nitration reaction activity orders indicated with “<”. Group (1) is benzoic acid structure PhCO2H < ethylbenzene structure PhCH2CH3 < phenol structure PhOH. Group (2) is another group of benzene-ring compounds containing substituents such as carboxyl, ethylamino, amino, and nitro groups. Reasoning: Nitration of aromatic rings belongs to electrophilic substitution reactions, and the influence of substituents on the electron cloud density of the benzene ring determines the ease of reaction. -CO2H is an electron-withdrawing group, which deactivates the benzene ring and makes nitration the most difficult; -CH2CH3 can weakly donate electrons through hyperconjugation, making the benzene ring more active than benzoic acid; -OH strongly donates electrons through resonance, significantly activating the benzene ring and making nitration the easiest. Therefore, the order PhCO2H < PhCH2CH3 < PhOH in group (1) is correct.

raw_record.question_text: The following two groups of reaction formulas represent the reaction order for nitration reactions of compounds. Please write the correct expression.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify option (1) as PhCO2H < PhCH2CH3 < PhOH and option (2) as another proposed sequence containing amino and nitro substituents. Then apply substituent electronic effects for nitration: -CO2H withdraws electrons and makes nitration hardest; -CH2CH3 donates weakly by hyperconjugation and is more reactive than benzoic acid; -OH strongly donates by resonance and is most reactive. Therefore the order in option (1) is correct, so write “(1)”.

method.method_draft: First describe the image options, noting that option (2) ends with or ranks PhNO2 as more readily nitrated than amino-substituted rings. Check this against electrophilic substitution principles: nitrobenzene is strongly deactivated by -NO2 and should not be placed as highly reactive toward nitration. Thus option (2) is inconsistent with nitration reactivity. Since the problem asks which of the two displayed orders is correct, eliminate (2) and choose “(1)”.
